text: In 2013, a new London skyscraper started cooking cars on the street.
Its face curves inward, like a giant concave mirror. On sunny days it focused sunlight onto the street below.
It got hot enough to warp parts of a parked Jaguar, and a reporter fried an egg on the pavement. Locals called it the Walkie-Scorchie. It got a permanent sunshade.
Curves make buildings beautiful. And dangerous to eggs.
